deed: יהודה פולקמן מגלה שגידולים סרטניים מגייסים כלי-דם ופותח דרך לתרופות חדשות
title: Judah Folkman discovered that cancerous tumors recruit blood vessels, and opened a path to new drugs

trailer.text: Judah Folkman, the son of a rabbi of Austrian-Jewish descent, was, according to Wikipedia, an American biologist and pediatric surgeon best known for his research on tumor angiogenesis, the process by which a tumor attracts blood vessels to nourish itself.
In 1971 he published a seminal paper in the New England Journal of Medicine, proposing that all tumor growth is angiogenesis-dependent.
According to Scientific American, for about two decades his peers treated him as a pariah and dismissed his theory, but he persisted with his research.
According to Nature Reviews Drug Discovery, in February 2004 the FDA approved bevacizumab for metastatic colorectal cancer, the first approval of a drug targeting tumor angiogenesis.
According to Folkman's obituary in the Harvard Gazette, at the time the obituary was published more than 1.2 million patients worldwide were receiving antiangiogenic therapy.

stations.title: The boy who accompanied his father the rabbi

paragraphs.text: Judah Folkman's father was a rabbi of Austrian-Jewish descent.
The son accompanied him on visits to hospital patients.
By age seven he knew he wanted to be a doctor rather than follow in his father's footsteps.
He wanted to offer patients cures, not only comfort.
At 19 he was accepted into Harvard Medical School.
According to the Harvard Gazette, while still a medical student, in Robert Gross's laboratory, Folkman and a colleague from MIT invented the first implantable heart pacemaker.

stations.title: In the Navy: tumors that stopped at a tiny size

paragraphs.text: In the middle of his residency at Massachusetts General Hospital, Folkman was suddenly drafted into the Navy.
He was assigned to research on artificial blood at a facility in Bethesda.
In these experiments, tiny tumors grew in glands kept outside the body.
According to the Harvard Gazette, all the little tumors were exactly the same size, and Folkman concluded that this was not natural.
The tumors did not die.
When they were transplanted back into mice, they rapidly acquired blood vessels and grew to a volume of more than 1 cubic centimeter.
According to Cancer World, in a living mouse they grew vigorously.
At the time, according to Cancer World, the prevailing cancer treatments were chemotherapy and radiation.
They indiscriminately killed both cancerous and non-cancerous cells.
Until the early 1970s, the accepted assumption was that the blood vessels in a tumor were an inflammatory reaction to dying tumor cells.
In 1967, at the age of 34, Folkman was appointed surgeon-in-chief of Children's Hospital Boston.
According to Wikipedia, he was the youngest full professor in the history of Harvard Medical School.
Alongside his work as surgeon-in-chief, he continued in the laboratory to develop the theories of angiogenesis.
In 1971 he published a paper in the New England Journal of Medicine proposing that all tumor growth is angiogenesis-dependent.
The paper introduced the term anti-angiogenesis, meaning the prevention of the sprouting of new blood vessels recruited by the tumor.
According to the Hebrew website "Big Science, in Brief", this is the hypothesis that tumors create a network of new blood vessels in order to grow beyond a tiny size.
In the 1970s, reviewers at the National Cancer Institute summarily turned down the team's first grant application.
The stated reason was that tumor growth cannot be dependent on blood vessel growth, any more than infection is dependent on pus.
At his first cancer conferences, most of the audience would get up and leave when he rose to speak.
One physician recalled that when he first heard of Folkman, he was described as someone working on an island in Boston Harbor.
In the laboratory he encountered "impossibles", such as the belief that blood vessel cells could not be grown in culture.
According to Scientific American, when his other funding sources dried up, Folkman was forced to take $23 million from the chemical company Monsanto.
According to Wikipedia, in 1974 Harvard and Monsanto signed a 10-year research grant.
The agreement yielded no products for Monsanto, and when it ended Folkman began receiving funding from Takeda.
Folkman and his team proved that tumors require blood to grow, and that they recruit blood vessel systems that bring them fresh blood.
The recruitment is carried out by hormone-like growth factors emitted by the tumor.
In 1971 the team isolated an angiogenic factor.
In the 1990s the laboratory discovered that two natural proteins, angiostatin and endostatin, could effectively block angiogenesis.
Both were discovered in the laboratory by a young postdoctoral fellow, Michael O'Reilly.
According to Wikipedia, angiostatin was discovered in 1991 as the first endogenous angiogenesis inhibitor, followed by endostatin, with Entremed funding.
In 1997 the group published experiments in which endostatin dramatically reduced aggressive malignant tumors by choking off their blood supply.
Other researchers in the laboratory found more inhibitors.
According to Wikipedia, Donald Ingber discovered that a fungus secretes fumagillin, a chemical that inhibits angiogenesis.
In 1994 Robert D'Amato discovered that thalidomide inhibits angiogenesis.
Genentech reported success with the drug Avastin, which blocks VEGF, one of the stimulators of blood vessel growth.
Clinical trials showed that regular infusions of Avastin extend the lives of patients with colorectal cancer.
According to the Hebrew article, Avastin is the first drug to be approved, and it contains an antibody that neutralizes VEGF.
According to Nature Reviews Drug Discovery, in February 2004 the FDA approved bevacizumab as a first-line treatment for metastatic colorectal cancer.
Thalidomide also reached patients.
Folkman convinced the doctor of a patient with multiple myeloma to try it, and in the trial that followed about a third of the subjects responded to the treatment.
In 2006 the FDA granted accelerated approval for thalidomide in combination with dexamethasone for newly diagnosed multiple myeloma patients.
According to Wikipedia, among the first clinical trials of angiogenesis inhibitors, Folkman and his colleagues treated infants with hemangiomas with interferon alpha.
The idea also reached the eyes.
According to the Harvard Gazette, research from the Folkman laboratory showed that anti-angiogenesis treatments can halt, and even reverse, wet macular degeneration.
Many of the patients are able to read smaller letters on the eye chart.
According to Wikipedia, a similar drug, Lucentis, was later approved for treating macular degeneration.
According to Cancer World, anti-angiogenic drugs have been approved for more than 25 types of cancer.
Folkman told BusinessWeek in 2005 that all his patients report having great strength and are returning to work.
According to the Harvard Gazette, Folkman was a member of the National Academy of Sciences, the Institute of Medicine and the American Philosophical Society, among other honorary appointments.
In 1992 he won Israel's Wolf Prize in Medicine.
According to Wikipedia, he also won Canada's Gairdner Award.
His work in the Navy also gave rise to another idea.
He noticed that plastic tubing gradually leaks oil-based fluids.
With a colleague at the National Naval Medical Center, he first reported the implantation of silicone polymers for the sustained release of drugs.
This led directly to the development of Norplant, a long-term contraceptive delivered via implanted plastic capsules.
Robert Langer, a chemical engineer, was among Folkman's first postdoctoral fellows, and according to the Harvard Gazette he is now an Institute Professor at MIT.
According to the JCI, Folkman offered to give three lectures in a course on tumor microcirculation, and did so for 16 years.
According to the JCI, he is known as the founder of the field of angiogenesis research, and is regarded as a caring physician, a brilliant scholar and an inspiring teacher.
On January 14, 2008, Folkman died suddenly of a heart attack at the Denver airport, at the age of 74.
He was on his way to deliver a keynote address at the Keystone Symposia in Vancouver.
He was survived by his wife, Paula Prial, two daughters and a granddaughter.
In 1998 Folkman became a media sensation when James Watson declared on the front page of The New York Times that Folkman would cure cancer within two years.
The stock price of EntreMed, the company licensed for angiostatin and endostatin, skyrocketed overnight.
According to the Harvard Gazette, fellow researchers reacted with anger and "animosity", and the publicity also led to doubts about Folkman's judgment.
In a 2002 interview, Folkman said that the news raised expectations and demand for the drugs before clinical trials had been completed.
Hints of efficacy were seen in Phase I trials, but the number of patients was small and the results not impressive.
In one trial, only four of 42 patients with cancers of hormone-producing nerve cells who were given endostatin experienced long-term relief.
Afterwards, funding for the trials essentially dried up, and no major pharmaceutical companies stepped forward to resume testing of endostatin and angiostatin.
Folkman was extremely upset at losing access to endostatin for his patients.
According to the review, the main problem in developing the drugs is that tumors may produce multiple angiogenic molecules.
According to Cancer World, VEGF treatment may cause bleeding, arterial blood clots, high blood pressure and delayed wound healing.

claims.quote: can be halted, and even reversed, by anti-angiogenesis treatments. Many of the patients treated with such drugs are able to read smaller letters on the eye charts

claims.text: לפי ויקיפדיה, תרופה דומה, לוסנטיס, אושרה מאוחר יותר לטיפול בניוון מקולרי.
claims.quote: A similar drug, Lucentis, was later approved for treating macular degeneration.

claims.text: לפי Cancer World, תרופות נוגדות אנגיוגנזה אושרו ליותר מ-25 סוגי סרטן.
claims.quote: It took until 2004 for that strategy to be developed and reach the clinic, with the approval of the first angiogenesis inhibitor, bevacizumab, in 2004

claims.text: לפי הארווארד גזט, יותר מ-10 מעכבי אנגיוגנזה אושרו על ידי ה-FDA, ותרופות כאלה אושרו ביותר מ-30 מדינות נוספות.
claims.quote: More than 10 angiogenesis inhibitors have been approved by the Food and Drug Administration, and anti-angiogenic drugs have received approvals in more than 30 other countries.

claims.text: פולקמן אמר ל-BusinessWeek ב-2005 שכל מטופליו מדווחים על כוח רב וחוזרים לעבודה.
claims.quote: All my patients comment on how much strength they have; they're all back at work.

claims.text: הארווארד גזט מציין שפולקמן היה חבר באקדמיה הלאומית למדעים, במכון לרפואה, באקדמיה האמריקאית לאמנויות ומדעים ובאגודה הפילוסופית האמריקאית.
claims.quote: Judah Folkman was a member of the National Academy of Sciences, the Institute of Medicine, the National Academy of Arts and Sciences, and the American Philosophical Society

claims.text: לפי ויקיפדיה, פולקמן זכה בין היתר בפרס וולף הישראלי ובפרס גרדנר הקנדי.
claims.quote: Canada's Gairdner Foundation International Award, Israel's Wolf Prize, Germany's Ernst Schering Prize

claims.text: במהלך עבודתו בצי שם לב פולקמן לכך שצינורות פלסטיק דולפים בהדרגה נוזלים על בסיס שמן.
claims.quote: While doing blood research for the Navy, Folkman had noticed that plastic tubing will gradually leak oil-based fluids

claims.text: פולקמן ועמית במרכז הרפואי הימי הלאומי דיווחו לראשונה על שימוש בפולימרים מסיליקון להשתלה לשחרור מתמשך של תרופות.
claims.quote: Folkman and a colleague at the National Naval Medical Center, Bethesda, MD, first reported the use of silicone rubber implantable polymers for the sustained release of drugs.

claims.text: הדבר הוביל ישירות לפיתוח נורפלנט, אמצעי מניעה ארוך טווח הניתן באמצעות כמוסות פלסטיק מושתלות.
claims.quote: It led directly to the development of Norplant, the long-term contraceptive that is delivered via implantable plastic capsules.

claims.text: רוברט לנגר, מהנדס כימי שהיה בין חוקרי הפוסט-דוקטורט הראשונים של פולקמן, הוא כיום פרופסור מכון ב-MIT.
claims.quote: One of his early postdoctoral fellows, chemical engineer Robert Langer, now an Institute Professor at MIT

claims.text: ג'יין מציין שפולקמן הציע להרצות שלוש הרצאות בקורס של ג'יין על מיקרו-סירקולציה של גידולים וכך עשה במשך 16 שנה.
claims.quote: He immediately accepted and offered to give not one but three lectures, which he continued to do for the next 16 years.

claims.text: לפי ג'יין (JCI), פולקמן ידוע כמייסד תחום חקר האנגיוגנזה, ונחשב רופא אכפתי, חוקר מבריק ומורה מעורר השראה.
claims.quote: Known widely as the founder of the field of angiogenesis research, he was a caring physician, a brilliant scholar, an inspiring teacher, and a true gentleman.

claims.text: יהודה פולקמן מת בפתאומיות ב-14 בינואר לאחר התקף לב בנמל התעופה הבינלאומי של דנוור, והיה בן 74.
claims.quote: died suddenly Monday (Jan. 14) after suffering a heart attack at the Denver International Airport in Denver. He was 74.

claims.text: פולקמן מת ב-14 בינואר 2008 בדרכו לשאת נאום מרכזי בסימפוזיון קיסטון בוונקובר.
claims.quote: Folkman died of a heart attack in Denver on January 14, 2008, at the age of 74 en route to deliver the 2008 Keynote Address at the Keystone Symposia

claims.text: פולקמן הותיר אישה, פאולה פריאל, שתי בנות ונכדה.
claims.quote: Folkman is survived by his wife, the former Paula Prial, with whom he lived in Brookline, Mass., two daughters, and one granddaughter.

claims.text: ב-1998 הפך פולקמן לסנסציה תקשורתית כשג'יימס ווטסון הצהיר בעמוד הראשון של ניו יורק טיימס שהוא מצפה שהסרטן ייפתר.
claims.quote: In 1998 Folkman became a media sensation when Nobel scientist James Watson, co-discoverer of the DNA double helix, declared on the front page of The New York Times

claims.text: חברת EntreMed שברשותה הרישיון לאנגיוסטטין ואנדוסטטין ראתה את מחיר מניותיה מזנק בן לילה.
claims.quote: the Maryland company licensed to make and test angiostatin and endostatin, EntreMed Inc., saw its stock price skyrocket overnight.

claims.text: הארווארד גזט מציין שחוקרים עמיתים הגיבו בכעס וב'טינה' לפרסום, שהוביל גם לספקות לגבי שיקול דעתו של פולקמן.
claims.quote: Animosity within the profession

claims.text: פולקמן אמר בראיון ב-2002 שהחדשות העלו ציפיות וביקוש לתרופות מעכבות אנגיוגנזה לפני שסיימו ניסויים קליניים.
claims.quote: raised expectations and demand for angiogenesis inhibitors before these drugs had completed testing in clinical trials.

claims.text: בניסויים קליניים בשלב I נראו רמזים ליעילות אך מספר החולים היה קטן והתוצאות לא מרשימות.
claims.quote: Hints of efficacy were seen in Phase I toxicity trials, but the number of patients was small and the results not impressive.

claims.text: בניסוי אחד רק ארבעה מתוך 42 חולים בסרטן של תאי עצב מייצרי הורמונים שקיבלו אנדוסטטין חוו הקלה ארוכת טווח.
claims.quote: including one in which only four of 42 patients suffering from cancers affecting hormone-producing nerve cells who were given endostatin experienced long-term relief.

claims.text: לאחר מכן המימון לניסויים קליניים כמעט התייבש, וחברות תרופות גדולות לא התגייסו לחדש את הבדיקות של אנדוסטטין ואנגיוסטטין.
claims.quote: the financial backing for clinical trials essentially dried up, and no major pharmaceutical firms stepped forward to resume clinical testing of endostatin and angiostatin.

claims.text: פולקמן היה נסער מאוד מכך שאיבד גישה לאנדוסטטין עבור מטופליו.
claims.quote: Folkman was extremely upset by losing access to endostatin for his patients.

claims.text: הבעיה העיקרית בפיתוח תרופות נוגדות אנגיוגנזה היא שגידולים עשויים לייצר מולקולות אנגיוגניות רבות.
claims.quote: The main problem in the development of antiangiogenic agents is that multiple angiogenic molecules may be produced by tumors

claims.text: לפי Cancer World, טיפול ב-VEGF עלול לגרום לדימום, קרישי דם בעורקים, לחץ דם גבוה וריפוי פצעים מעוכב.
claims.quote: Treatment with VEGF- targeting angiogenesis inhibitors may result in bleeding, arterial clots, high blood pressure, delayed wound healing

claims.text: לפי WBUR (על בסיס ביוגרפיה של בית החולים), מעכבי אנגיוגנזה אושרו ב-FDA לסרטן ולניוון מקולרי ואושרו גם ב-27 מדינות נוספות.
claims.quote: angiogenesis inhibitors have received FDA approval in the U.S. for cancer and for the treatment of macular degeneration and are also approved in 27 other countries.
